rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the waiting period, the Prophet proposed to Zaynab through Zayd; she accepted after istikhārah, her brother solemnized the marriage, and the dower was 400 dirhams with a lavish wedding banquet.
rows.anchor: Her brother, Abū Aḥmad ibn Jaḥash solemnized this marriage. The Prophet (sws) fixed the dower at 400 dirhams and threw a very elaborate wedding banquet

rows.speaker: some people
rows.claim: Some infer from zawwajna that the marriage occurred in heaven and required no earthly ceremony.
rows.anchor: Some people have concluded from the word اَن ْجَّوَز that the wedding took place in the heavens and no need arose to have it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi rejects the heavenly-wedding inference: Ibn Hishām records the marriage details, and it followed the marriage method prescribed by God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: Hence, the correct version of this incident is that at the behest of God, this marriage was conducted

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When reforming the jāhiliyyah custom, God had it corrected at the appointed time by His prescribed method, and opponents could not obstruct His plan.
rows.anchor: when the time came for the reformation of this jāhiliyyah custom, it was set right at that time according to the divinely prescribed methodology

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's difficult life phases are neither unique nor cause for discomfort: earlier messengers faced them under God's established practice and wisdom.
rows.anchor: All previous messengers have also passed through them. This is an established practice of God which He has fixed in accordance with His wisdom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such divinely ordained trials instruct and test messengers, exposing their capacities and the sincerity or insincerity of their followers.
rows.anchor: These tests bring to the fore their hidden potentials and the sincerity or the lack of it on the part of their followers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression ‘God ordained for him’ means that God set circumstances for someone; ‘God made obligatory upon him’ means He imposed a duty.
rows.anchor: The latter means that God has made something obligatory on someone while the former means that God has ordained certain circumstances for someone.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi says the compressed Qur’anic sentence uses a style found earlier; supplying its suppressed parts yields a statement of God's established rule for His prophets.
rows.anchor: If all the suppressed parts of this sentence are accounted

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reconstructed phrase means this is God's established practice prescribed for His prophets.
rows.anchor: This is an established practice prescribed by God for His prophets

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God fixed the time for carrying out His decision; life does not happen by chance, so believers should face events as faith requires.
rows.anchor: nothing in life occurs by chance. It occurs in accordance with the program set for it by God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier prophets conveyed God's messages without fearing anyone but Him; Muhammad likewise must fulfill this duty despite reproach.
rows.anchor: they would communicate the messages of God and they never cared for anyone in this matter other than God.

rows.speaker: Ibn Kathīr and al-Zamakhsharī
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and al-Zamakhsharī interpret ḥasīb as ‘helper,’ making the close mean that God suffices to protect people from dangers.
rows.anchor: Ibn Kathīr and al- Zamakhsharī76 are of the opinion that the word بۡیِسَح in َو اًبۡی ِT Tسَ حِ ّٰللّٰہاِی بٰفَک means “helper.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ḥasīb means one who takes account, the verse warns that God will call to account anyone who neglects conveying His message out of fear or deference.
rows.anchor: if this word is interpreted in its general meaning of “someone who takes account,” then this part of the verse will serve as a warning.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse answers those who claimed Muhammad was Zayd's father: he is father to no man, but God's Messenger and the seal of the Prophets.
rows.anchor: The verse states that Muḥammad (sws) is father to no man

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Muhammad is the final prophet and religion is completed through him, the reform of this custom and every deviant practice had to occur through him.
rows.anchor: since he is also the last of the prophets, it is essential that this evil custom be reformed through him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should judge the matter by the Prophet's true status and mission, not hypothetical claims; he must act as God directs despite reproach, and deniers face God's established punishment.
rows.anchor: it should be viewed in the light of his real position and status and the responsibility it entails.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording broadens the correction from denying that Muhammad fathered Zayd to saying he fathered no man; his male children died in infancy and were not technically men.
rows.anchor: the words actually say that he is father to no man. This has added stress in the whole statement

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger is always a prophet, while a prophet need not be a messenger; therefore, Muhammad's being the final prophet also makes him the final messenger.
rows.anchor: Every messenger (rasūl) is always a prophet (nabī) but the reverse is not necessarily true.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi rejects the sectarian claim that naming Muhammad the final prophet leaves some aspects of messengerhood open, calling it ignorance.
rows.anchor: and hence this does not terminate all components of messengerhood. However, this view is based on mere ignorance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lexicographers treat khātam and khātim as synonymous; either can mean the last person in a group, a thing's end, or a letter's seal.
rows.anchor: It can connote the last person of a community, the fate of a thing and the seal at the end of a letter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who caused the dispute should recognize that God knows more than they do about Zayd, Zaynab, the Messenger, and their relationships.
rows.anchor: those who have created all this rumpus should know that God is more aware of

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything happened with God's knowledge and permission; protesting is ignorant, faith requires trusting His wisdom, and only His comprehensive knowledge grasps the corrective act's subtleties.
rows.anchor: Whatever happened was at His behest and permission. Hence, creating commotion against this is mere ignorance and foolishness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against hypocrites' and mischief-makers' opposition, believers should disregard the uproar and increase remembrance and praise of God by night and day.
rows.anchor: while disregarding their rumpus they should engage more and more in remembering God and in extolling Him by night and by day.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's remembrance is believers' shield against Satan; Qur'anic calls to persevere against enemies repeatedly direct believers to prayer, whose link to perseverance is discussed elsewhere in the tafsīr.
rows.anchor: the real shield through which believers have to counter the onslaught of Satan and his progeny is God’s remembrance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ‘glorify Him morning and evening,’ prayer is the specific after the general: remembrance is constant, while God and His Messenger set prayer times within this morning-evening timetable.
rows.anchor: Here حیتسب symbolizes the prayer. It is in fact the mention of the specific after the general.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends mercy upon believers, while angels pray for God to grant them mercy.
rows.anchor: He sends down His mercy on His believers and His angels too continue to pray to God to grant His mercy to the believers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's darkness means darkness of belief and its light means guidance; its close describes God as merciful to believers.
rows.anchor: darkness obviously refers to the darkness of beliefs and light refers to the light of guidance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusallī means God's mercy when attributed to God and angels' prayer for mercy when attributed to angels; 33:56 illustrates the distinction, and the close here signals God's mercy to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: The word یۡ ِّلَصُی when used with reference to God will allude to His mercy and when used with reference to the angels will mean their prayer for mercy.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi cites angels' prayers for forgiveness of believers in Sūrah al-Mu’min and Sūrah al-Shūrā.
rows.anchor: The fact that angels seek forgiveness for the believers is mentioned at other places in the Qur’ān as well.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing God's worldly mercy, the passage says believers will meet God in the Hereafter with a greeting of peace and an honourable reward.
rows.anchor: when these people will meet their Lord in the Hereafter, they will be greeted with the salutation of salām and God would have prepared for them a very honourable recompense.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taḥiyyah is attached to its object and means ‘greeting’; other Qur'anic passages likewise describe Paradise's residents receiving salām from God and angels.
rows.anchor: The word ٌةَّیِحَت is affixed to its object and its correct meaning is “greeting.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic examples describe the people of Paradise welcomed with greetings and peace by God and angels or the keepers of Paradise.
rows.anchor: the dwellers of Paradise will receive salām (peace) from God and the angels too will greet them by these words.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses clarify the Prophet's position and duties to him and his audience: as witness, he testifies to God's commands and to conduct that earns God's pleasure; this is a messenger's central purpose.
rows.anchor: The word ًدِاہَش means someone who bears witness to the directives of God and to the attitude that earns His pleasure.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet gives glad tidings to those accepting his message and warns those rejecting it; after that his witnessing duty is complete, while acceptance and its sincerity belong to God.
rows.anchor: The expression اًرۡیِذَ ن َّا و ًرِّشَبُم means that the Prophet (sws) should give glad tidings to people who accept his message

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's permission explains the Prophet's call toward Him and assures him that, as God's appointed messenger rather than a self-styled prophet, he will receive help and succeed despite opposition.
rows.anchor: since God Himself has appointed him to call people towards God, He will not leave the Prophet (sws) alone.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is a shining lamp lit by knowledge and wisdom, guiding others from darkness; those who fail to value him only hasten their own worldly and ultimate ruin.
rows.anchor: God has made the Prophet (sws) a shinning lamp which is lit up with the radiance of knowledge and wisdom and will also bring others out from darkness
